title: Document 1 — Visitor notice | Larch Bay Sand Day
titleZh: 文件 1｜遊客公告｜落葉松灣沙雕日
passage:
This year's sculptures will stand on low platforms in the sand. A yellow cord marks the public route; a blue cord marks the work area for teams repairing sculptures. The yellow route will remain open even while some teams are working. Wooden viewing mats are available at the west entrance for visitors who prefer a firm surface.

The shapes of three entries look very different from their two marked sides. For those entries, every visitor vote has two boxes: choose the side you looked from, then mark the shape you liked. You do not need to look from both sides. If rain blurs a viewing mark, a steward will point to the correct viewing spot; do not stand inside the blue cord to make the shape easier to recognize.

The west platform will be repaired at noon. The public route still reaches it from the east. Its west viewing mark will be covered by a temporary board, but the steward beside the mat can still direct visitors to both marked sides from the public route. A steward will collect paper votes at the exit; we will not collect votes inside the marked work area. At the west-platform entry, the shapes really do look different from the two marked spots. For the trial, cards that say ‘Ask at the mat’ mean the steward takes you to the western spot, even if you arrive on the public route from the east. Cards that say ‘Follow the gull flags’ lead to the eastern spot. In full sun, a thin ridge on the sculpture is hard to see even from a marked spot. The noon repair screen will shade the whole sculpture until we take it down for the closing photograph. We will put it back up for the closing walk.

Stewards may suggest either viewing spot when visitors ask, but they do not direct equal numbers to each side. A visitor can vote only after seeing the sculpture, and can also walk away without voting. The display at the exit will list the votes by the side marked on each ballot. It will not list how many visitors stood on each side, including those who did not vote. After voting ends, first-time viewers can help us try out next year’s directions. Fern-card volunteers will hear ‘Look for a fan’ and will ask at the mat as the photographer arrives, before we take the screen down. Shell-card volunteers will ask at the mat while the photographer is taking pictures. Pebble-card volunteers will follow the gull flags during the closing walk. Reed-card volunteers will ask at the mat during that walk. Only Fern cards give the fan hint; the other cards simply ask what shape the volunteers see. Their replies will not be entered as votes.
passageZh:
今年的沙雕會放在沙地裡的低平台上。黃色繩索標示遊客動線，藍色繩索標示各隊修補沙雕的工作區。即使有參賽隊還在作業，黃色動線也維持開放。若希望走在較硬的表面上，可在西側入口使用木製觀覽墊。

三座參賽沙雕從標示的兩側看，形狀差異很大。這三座作品的票上都有兩個要填的欄位：先選你從哪一側看，再標記你喜歡的造型。你不必從兩側都看過。如果下雨讓觀覽位置的標記模糊，引導員會指出正確的觀覽點；不要為了更容易辨認造型而站到藍繩內。

西側平台會在中午進行修補。遊客動線仍可從東側通往該處。西側的觀覽位置標記會被臨時木板蓋住，但觀覽墊旁的引導員仍能指示遊客從公開動線前往兩側的觀覽點。出口會有引導員收紙本選票；工作區內不收票。 西側平台這座作品從兩處標示的觀覽點望去，形狀確實不同。試行時，卡片上寫「在觀覽墊旁詢問」，表示由引導員帶你去西側觀覽點，即使你是從東側沿公開動線過來也一樣。寫「沿海鷗旗前進」的卡片則會帶你到東側觀覽點。日照強時，即使站在標示的觀覽點，也不容易看見沙雕上一道細細的稜線。中午修補時架起的遮陽布會遮住整座作品，直到拍攝閉幕照片時才拆下；閉幕巡覽時會再架回去。

遊客詢問時，引導員可以建議任一個觀覽點，但不會刻意安排兩側人數相等。遊客要先看過沙雕才能投票，也可以看完就離開、不投票。 出口看板會依每張選票所填的觀覽側別列出得票，但不會列出各側的觀覽人數，包括看過卻沒有投票的人。 投票結束後，還沒看過這座作品的遊客可以自願協助試行明年的觀覽指引。拿蕨葉卡的志工會聽到「找找看扇子的形狀」，並在攝影師抵達、遮陽布尚未拆下時，到觀覽墊旁詢問。拿貝殼卡的人在攝影師拍照時到觀覽墊旁詢問。拿小石卡的人在閉幕巡覽時沿海鷗旗前進；拿蘆葦卡的人也在巡覽時到觀覽墊旁詢問。只有蕨葉卡會提到扇子的提示；其他卡片只問志工看見什麼形狀。志工的回答不計入選票。
